intro.narration: [excited] Eighty percent off — sixty-eight pounds. [pause] What was it before?

steps.narration: [curious] You know the sale price. [pause] You want the ticket price.
[confident] Eighty off means you keep twenty percent. [pause] Divide by that.
[excited] Dividing by zero point two is times five. Sixty-eight times five is three hundred and forty.
[confident] Three hundred and forty pounds. [pause] Take eighty percent off — sixty-eight.
[thoughtful] One catch: a hundred percent off. [pause] You keep nothing, so there is nothing to divide by.

timing.note: Every 'seconds' value is the ffprobe measurement printed by core/tools/elevenlabs.mjs, used verbatim. total_seconds = measured audio (40.72) + the ~1.3 s of hand-off, card-in and cross-fade transitions. Each step holds for exactly its clip length; no clip is stretched or compressed.

voice.clips: one request per step plus one for the intro, cached by hash of (text, voice, model, settings); the pre-recorded assets/audio/start_audio/* greetings are not used

plan_fidelity.note: Display copy is the plan's instruction and working lines used as-is, character for character, including the ✓ and ✗ glyphs and the U+2212 minus signs. No number, formula, applicability condition, carry case, step order or counter was altered. The narration paraphrases only; it never states a number the plan does not state.

nulls.reason: Not used by design: §5.4 of the brief requires the lesson intro to be generated with the rest of the narration so the post is one performance in one voice.

The spoken script does not read the plan's full applicability clause (all real P > 0, all 0 ≤ d < 100, exactness, the S·(1 + d/100) < P failure bound). It is far too long for a 60 s post, and abridging it in speech would weaken a condition the Verifier checks in full. The audible lesson carries the rule, the worked example and the d = 100 caveat; the unspoken conditions are neither contradicted nor implied to be absent.

carry_case names two failures: d = 100 (division by zero, the information is gone) and the common wrong move of adding the discount back (68 × 1.8 = £122.40). Only the first is spoken, on card s5, because it is the one the plan gave a card to. The second is carried by step s3's own instruction line, 'Divide, don't add back', used as-is; the £122.40 figure appears on no card in the plan and was not added to one here.

Nothing is said about stripping VAT (÷ 1.2) or about undoing two stacked discounts. The plan explicitly declines to assert either (nulls[0] and nulls[1]); mentioning them in narration would assert them by implication.

tooling_note: Clips were produced by core/tools/elevenlabs.mjs say() via its module API (driver: tts-driver.mjs in this run directory). The documented CLI form exits 0 with no output on this host because the file's `import.meta.url === file://${process.argv[1]}` guard never matches a Windows argv path — the same guard failure the planner recorded for ledger.mjs and sampling.mjs. No HTTP was hand-rolled and no credential was read, printed or written by this agent.
